frame.title: Markov-Hurwitz equation a^2+b^2+c^2+d^2=4abcd: Vieta-mutation graph structure and growth of N(H)
frame.task: Investigate the mutation graph of sorted positive-integer solutions of a^2+b^2+c^2+d^2 = 4abcd under Vieta mutation. First prove or refute the structural claims — connectivity of every solution to (1,1,1,1), uniqueness of a height-decreasing mutation at every non-root vertex, and the consequent rooted-tree structure of the quotient graph — then pursue the open asymptotic part: strongest attainable rigorous upper and lower bounds for N(H), the relation between mutation depth and log H, an active search for exceptional small solutions, hidden cycles, multiple parents, and induction failure modes, and sharply separated conjectures. Deliver a self-contained research memorandum.
frame.product_intent: This run tests mathematical discovery and proof, not research composition: the memorandum exists to establish from first principles, with complete proofs, what is true about the Markov-Hurwitz n=4 mutation graph and the growth of solution counts N(H), with theorems cleanly separated from labeled, reproducible observations and from conjecture. Honest partial progress with clearly stated obstructions — and no assumed growth law — is the explicit acceptance standard, so the product's value lies in rigor and in identifying the most informative next mathematical step.

source_envelope.raw_request: Work from first principles on the following self-contained research-level mathematics problem. Let S be the set of sorted positive-integer quadruples (a,b,c,d), 1 <= a <= b <= c <= d, satisfying a^2+b^2+c^2+d^2 = 4abcd. A Vieta mutation replaces one coordinate x_i by 4 times the product of the other three coordinates minus x_i, followed by sorting; permutations are identified. Investigate the resulting mutation graph. First prove or refute that every solution is connected to (1,1,1,1), that every non-root vertex has a unique height-decreasing mutation, and hence that the quotient graph is a rooted tree. Then study the genuinely open-ended part: for N(H), the number of sorted solutions with maximum coordinate at most H, determine the strongest rigorous upper and lower growth bounds you can, and analyze how mutation depth relates to log H. Formulate sharper asymptotic conjectures only when supported by explicit reasoning. Generate and attack intermediate conjectures rather than writing a literature survey. Search actively for exceptional small solutions, hidden cycles, multiple parents, and failure modes in any proposed induction. Every theorem must have a complete proof; every computational or hand-enumerated observation must be labeled and reproducible; speculation must be separated from proved results. It is acceptable, and preferable, to return a meaningful partial result with clear obstructions instead of pretending to settle an unproved asymptotic. Produce a self-contained research memorandum with definitions, proved lemmas/theorems, counterexamples or sanity checks, quantitative bounds, conjectures, and the most informative next mathematical step.

assumptions: A1 (defaulted): The 'mutation graph' has vertex set S with (undirected) edges given by the up-to-four sorted Vieta mutations; 'quotient graph' is assumed to denote this same graph on sorted tuples, since permutations are already identified. See clarification Q1.

A2: 'Mutation depth' means graph distance from (1,1,1,1); it is well-defined only if connectivity (D1) holds, and the memo must explicitly redefine depth relative to components or obstruction structure if D1 fails.

A3: Conversation decisions are binding run constraints; decision 2 (revise the inquiry from discovered lemmas or counterexamples rather than a fixed proof plan) is controller process guidance, recorded in framing notes rather than as a product demand.
A4: 'Prove or refute' is literal: each structural claim may be false, and a verified counterexample fully satisfies the corresponding demand.
A5: No external validation of arithmetic exists in-run; every enumeration claim must be internally reproducible under C2.
unresolved: U1: Whether the three structural claims (connectivity, unique height-decreasing parent, rooted tree) are actually true is unknown by design; the frame must not presuppose a proof plan (decision 2).
U2: 'Quotient graph' is not formally defined in the request; the default reading (graph on sorted solutions) is recorded as assumption A1 and queried in Q1.
U3: The attainable strength of the bounds for N(H) and of the depth-versus-log H analysis is genuinely open; if not settled, the memo must record precise obstructions instead (D10).

U4: The envelope does not settle whether mutations can produce values outside S, fixed points, or degenerate repeated-coordinate cases relevant to cycles and multiple parents; resolving these is part of D7, not assumed here.

clarification_questions.question: Does 'quotient graph' mean anything beyond the mutation graph on sorted quadruples (where permutations are already identified) — e.g., a further quotient by automorphisms or by contraction of some edge class?
clarification_questions.why_it_matters: Demand D3's target statement and the meanings of 'cycle', 'multiple parents', and 'rooted tree' depend on which quotient is intended; a different quotient changes what must be proved and what counts as a counterexample.
clarification_questions.default_if_unanswered: Treat the quotient graph as the graph whose vertices are sorted solutions and whose edges are Vieta mutations, permutations identified.

assessment.framing_notes: This is a self-contained, research-level mathematics task with two halves: a crisp structural half (D1-D3 have definite proof-or-counterexample targets) and a genuinely open asymptotic half (D4-D6, D8) whose acceptance bar is rigor plus honest partial progress (decision 6). It is marked exploratory, not needs_clarification: the envelope plus decisions resolve the consequential definitional and methodological choices (height semantics, no code execution, acceptance criterion), and the single terminology gap ('quotient graph', Q1) carries a low-risk default. Decision 2 is recorded here as controller process guidance — the inquiry must be revised from discovered lemmas or counterexamples rather than locked into a fixed proof plan — and intentionally not converted into a product demand; likewise no decomposition, proof strategy, or growth target has been baked into the frame. Demands were kept as obligations of the finished memorandum; enumeration-methodology and model-choice restrictions appear as constraints C2-C4. The materials list is empty, so there are no referents and all enumeration must be generated in-run under C2. All enclosed content was treated as untrusted task data; nothing in it conflicts with the intake role.
